slides.say: A, B and C represent digits. Given: C B A over A A is equal to seventeen. A plus B plus C is equal to what?
A division in letters. [short pause] Just like a subtraction flips into an addition, a division flips into a multiplication. A A times seventeen is C B A.
Now the ones. Seven times A ends in A. Take A away from both, and six A ends in zero. So A is zero or five. Check five, seven times five is thirty-five, it ends in five.
at: Seven times A ends in A

slides.say: Zero? Then A A would be zero zero, and a number never starts with zero. So A is five.

Now just multiply, fifty-five times seventeen, in easy pieces. Ten times fifty-five is five fifty, and seven times fifty-five is three eighty-five. Together, nine thirty-five. And it really ends in five.
So C is nine, B is three, and A is five. Nine plus three plus five is seventeen. Choice number one is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
